1- SAC code in SLI (for WVPC only) , if this field has a code in it, it needs to be removed.

1-On GIS, go to documents- choose consignment\\invoices of chassis

5- If not, then it's not on a demo funding

articles.title: Negotiated:
articles.html:
Negotiated:

  • The vehicle belongs to another retailer.
  • The requesting retailer must contact the owning retailer to get permission for an internal transfer.
  • If they cannot transfer it directly, the owning retailer must submit a transfer form.

Mandatory (National stock):

  • The vehicle is in the owning retailer's account tagged as stock and will show as mandatory
  • If a consignment request is pending, the vehicle is locked until requested consignment is complete.
  • The retailer who asked for the mandatory car must tag the vehicle immediately upon consignment to secure it.
  • If it's fully consigned and untagged any one can take it from this retailer without a form or a permission as long as it shows mandatory

For Škoda vehicles in the national stock where the RDC starts with a 3 (e.g., 31959), requests cannot be made via phone or e-forms. They must email these requests directly to vehiclesupport@skoda.co.uk.

Mandatory will show available when doing a Stock query search in SLI, as long as it's 07-Stock, it's fine to transfer to their account.

If for any reason the RDC provides the VIN and the vehicle is 06-Showroom (Even if it shows Mandatory in SLI) this cannot be allocated to the retailer.

articles.title: Handling Status 70 Error (Drop Point Issue) During Quotation
articles.html:
Overview

A Status 70 - Drop Point Issue typically occurs when the vehicle is already in transit or at the retailer. This usually happens when the standard quotation process is attempted first.

To successfully process the quotation, the vehicle must temporarily be moved back to Status 40, the quotation completed, and then Business Support should be contacted to update the vehicle status as required.

Prerequisites

Before starting:

  • Confirm the vehicle is showing Status 70.
  • Ensure you have the required RFO details available.
  • Follow the steps below in the exact order.

Step 1: Change the Vehicle Back to Status 40

1. Open Vehicle Status Management

Select the Red Truck icon to access the vehicle status functions.

[screenshot in Notion]

2. Cancel the Arrival Date

  • Right-click within the status management area.
  • Select Cancellation of Arrival Date.

[screenshot in Notion]

3. Cancel Dispatch to Retailer

After cancelling the arrival date:

  • Select Cancellation of Despatch to Retailer.

[screenshot in Notion]

4. Verify Status Change

  • Return to the Red Car icon (Vehicle Details).
  • Refresh the vehicle repeatedly until the status updates (using the binoculars icon).

The vehicle should now display Status 40.

Step 2: Prepare the Vehicle for Quotation

1. Open Order Modification

Once the vehicle is at Status 40:

  • Right-click the vehicle.
  • Select Order Modification.

[screenshot in Notion]

2. Re-Tag the Vehicle

  • Re-tag the vehicle as required to enable quotation processing.

3. Refresh the Record

After re-tagging, refresh the vehicle.

The vehicle will usually revert to Status 07.

For quotation processing, it must be Status 08/09. Update the Del. Add (Retailer location) to prepare for quotation.

[screenshot in Notion]

4. Change Order Type

Update the order type from 07 to 08.

Once updated, click the Yellow Quote button.

Step 3: Create the Quotation

1. Select Purchase Order Option

Within the quotation screen, choose TBC from the PO dropdown/menu.

2. Enter RFO Information

Complete the required fields: First RFO, Second RFO. Then click the Search icon.

[screenshot in Notion]

3. Continue the Standard Quotation Process

Once the search results are returned, proceed with the normal quotation workflow. All remaining quotation steps should be completed as per standard process.

Final Action

After the quotation has been successfully completed: Email Business Support and request that the vehicle status be updated appropriately following the quotation process.

Notes

Note: Always revert the vehicle to Status 40 before attempting the quotation when a Status 70 Drop Point Issue is encountered. After re-tagging, ensure the order is moved back to Status 08 before generating the quote. Do not proceed with quotation while the vehicle remains in Status 70.

articles.title: Agency Steps to De-Tag
articles.html:
For the de-tag step-by-step workflow, see Steps to De-Tag A Vehicle.

SLI - Agency Steps to De-Tag & Deallocate

Module Objective: Master the Agency De-Tag procedures based on status codes, brand rules, deallocation steps, handling date error workarounds, and cancelling commissions.

Brand & Status Code De-Tag Matrix

VWPC: Status 0-10: Detag, Deallocate & cancel commission. Status 20-38: Detag, Deallocate - DONT cancel commission. Status 38-40 (without Transport Order): Detag & Deallocate. Status 40-70 (with Transport Order): Forward sell the vehicle 150 days from the date arrived in the UK first, then Detag. Evidence for Status 20+: RDC must provide at least one: Cancellation document, Original order/Motability cancellation screenshot, VWFS finance decline letter, or Original agreement form.

VWCV: All statuses: Detag but DONT de-allocate. Status 40-70: Forward sell 150 days from UK arrival, then Detag. Status 10 or below: No evidence needed. Status 20+: Order form or Cancellation form. Reject ID.BUZZ at any status and ask them to fill in the correct form.

SKODA: Status 0-10: Detag, Deallocate & cancel commission. Status 20-38: Detag, Deallocate - DONT cancel commission. Status 38-40: Detag & Deallocate. Status 40-70: Forward sell 150 days from UK arrival, then Detag. Refer to HUB article SK1009-18.

SEAT/CUPRA: Same pattern as Skoda. Refer to HUB article SE0187-22.

Audi: Order types 08, 09, 11 - Status 0-10: Detag and Transfer to 64001. Status 20-38: Detag, Transfer to 64001 for status 30 and under. Status 38-40: Detag and add Mandatory Block EDE for 24 hours. Status 40-70: Detag and leave a note. No evidence needed.

Forward Sale Date Process (Status 40-70 with Transport Order)

When de-tagging vehicles with an active transport order (status 40-70), apply a forward sale date set 150 days after the arrival in the UK date.

Standard Process

  1. Right-click on the grey area and select Inform Forward Sale Date. [screenshot in Notion]
  2. Open a date calculator and enter the arrival in the UK date from SLI as the start date.
  3. Add 150 days to derive the new date.
  4. Input the calculated date into the Forward Sale Date Entry pop-up box and click Accept. [screenshot in Notion]
  5. Proceed with the standard de-tag procedure.

Handling the "Date Out of Range" Error

If SLI displays: Operation Result - CAR: [VIN] Forward Sale Date [YYYYMMDD] out of range [screenshot in Notion]

  1. Click Accept to dismiss the alert.
  2. In the Forward Sale Date Entry field, enter today's date first and click Accept.
  3. Open the menu again, re-select "Inform Forward Sale Date", and now enter "Today's Date + 150 days".
  4. Click Accept to save the forward sale date, then complete the De-Tag.

How to Deallocate a Vehicle Order

When your brand/status matrix specifies Deallocate:

  1. Open the vehicle record in SLI.
  2. Right-click in the top section of the screen to bring up the context menu.
  3. Click on Vehicle order deallocation. [screenshot in Notion]
  4. Select the appropriate unassigned reason (e.g., CUSTOMER CANCELLATION). [screenshot in Notion]
  5. Configure Options: At the bottom row of the screen, check both the Cancel order and Cancel commission checkboxes (if you want to remove the commission). [screenshot in Notion]
  6. Initiate Deallocation: Click the Deallocation button at the bottom right. [screenshot in Notion]
  7. Select Order Cancellation Reason: In the Choose Reason for Order Cancellation window, select CC - CUSTOMER CANCELLATION and click Accept. [screenshot in Notion]
  8. Select Commission Cancellation Reason: In the Choose a reason for the commissions' cancellation window, select BK - Commission cancellation and click Accept to finalize the process. [screenshot in Notion]

Step 1: Locate Order & Open Customer Details

  2. Click the customer icon (an icon featuring a person next to a document/file). [screenshot in Notion]

articles.html:
What You'll Learn

After this module: accurately read a Shipping Plan, list the uses for Shipping Plans, identify the different types of transportation, state the timescales for transportation.

The Three Stages of Transportation

Once a vehicle completes the Build phase and is ready to leave the factory, it moves through three stages on its way to the UK:

  1. Factory to Port of Exit (PSC 30-38): the vehicle travels to the ship on a vehicle transportation truck. Takes approximately 20 working days (maximum).
  2. Port of Exit to UK Port (PSC 38-39): this leg happens by ship. The timeframe varies depending on where the vehicle is leaving from.
  3. Port to Retailer (PSC 40-60): a vehicle transportation company delivers the car to the RDC. Can take up to 14 working days from the point the Transport Order is raised.

Note: Many factors can impact the full journey. A compound entry date needs to be raised. If a Transport Order is raised before the compound entry date, this can cause an issue. If a retailer calls asking where their car is, call the port to check if it's on their transport list. If the Transport Order is older than 10 days, escalate to a specialist.

Shipping Plans

A Shipping Plan lists every vessel leaving the port of exit, including departure dates, expected arrival dates at the port of entry, ship names, and the number of vehicles onboard.

  • International Plan: updated weekly, found on The Hub.
  • European Plan: updated daily, sent to the Specialist Inbox and shared with everyone.

RDCs use these plans as a guide to know when a vehicle is likely to arrive, or what stage of transportation it's at, and to set customers' expectations around their handover date.

Shipping Plan Status Codes

  • 00: Assigned to Factory, no production week scheduled
  • 10: Factory ordered with production week
  • 20: Factory ordered with production week confirmed
  • 30: In transit from Factory
  • 36: Vehicle in port of exit, not released
  • 38: Vehicle in port of exit, released to shipping
  • 39: Vehicle on ship
  • 40: Vehicle landed in UK, Transport order raised
  • 60: Dispatched to Retailer
  • 70: At Retailer
  • P: Not accepted by factory
  • V: Accepted by factory, awaiting build week assignment

Tools to use: VIP or ECM Portal. In ECM Portal, go to the Commission tab, load the VC OR Detail screen to view the ship's name. Alternatively, use the Road Icon from the Vehicle Detailed Information Screen.

What Is a Change of Funder?

If a Fleet Company is purchasing a vehicle, it will have its own RFO code in SLI. If the vehicle is not going to that fleet company and requires de-tagging instead, this is treated as a Change of Funder request. This is a similar process to standard De-tagging - the key difference is that the Detag reason on the E-form must state it is a Change of Funder request.

Steps

  2. Enter the Order number under Vehicle information.
  3. Check the RDC matches on both the E-form and SLI.
  4. Right-click on the grey area of the screen and select Order Modification.
  5. Select the Customer Entry tab, then check the current RFO and compare it to the information on the E-form (End user tab). [screenshot in Notion]
  6. Identify which RFO to change: usually only the second RFO number under the End User tab, as the Leasing Company usually stays the same.
  7. Update the RFO number under the End User tab to the one mentioned in the E-form.
  8. Select Save.
  9. Under the Dates tab, select the pen and scroll icon to leave a note. The note must include: Change of Funder (type of request, e.g. Agency/Leasing), the date, your initials. Select Modify to save the note.

articles.title: How to Perform a Stock Match
articles.html:
What Is a Stock Match?

A stock match happens when an RDC finds a different vehicle for a customer than the one they originally ordered, usually because a comparable vehicle is already further along in the build process, so the customer can take delivery sooner.

When an RDC locates a stock match, they should tag the customer to the new vehicle and complete the Stock Match Form on The Hub. Both orders, old and new, should now be tagged to the customer. Once the stock match form comes in, open the order in SLI and check that both orders are tagged to the same customer. From there: de-tag the old vehicle, price back the new vehicle to reflect the original pricing.

Brand-Specific Rules

  • Volkswagen Commercial Vehicles & Volkswagen Passenger Cars: the Stock Match can be for a different vehicle, as long as the customer stays the same. The replacement can be further forward or further back in build status than the original, e.g. if the customer wants to delay delivery.
  • Audi: stricter rules apply - the replacement must be the same model and trim (color can differ), and its build status must be further forward than the original order. Customer details must match.
  • Skoda: per the Matrix, if the replacement vehicle is further back in the build process (e.g. the customer wants to delay delivery), a letter or email is required as proof.

Step-by-Step: Performing a Stock Match in SLI

  1. Open two SLI windows side by side, one showing the original order and one showing the new (stock match) order.
  2. Click the Customer Tab on each order to confirm the same customer is listed on both. Make a note of the date the original vehicle was tagged (the input date) - needed in step 3. Note: if the new car's registration status is Partially (P/z/c), the process cannot continue.
  3. On the new order, click the yellow telephone icon, then click the pound sign to jump into pricing. Click the Re-pricing tab and change the VAL date to the original input date from step 2. This keeps the pricing shown to the customer matched to what they originally agreed to, not today's price.
  4. Click Simulation to run the updated pricing, then click Save to confirm. Once the new vehicle is priced back, go to the original vehicle's order and de-tag it using the standard de-tag process, keeping the evidence.

articles.title: VIP (Vehicle Information Portal) Guide

What is the VIP Portal?

VIP is the tracking system used to monitor vehicle delivery once a unit has arrived at a UK port.

  • Stock Pot Visibility: while retailers have access to the VIP portal, they cannot view full details for vehicles held within the stock pot. If they require this information, they may contact the Customer Service Centre (CSC).
  • Key information available in VIP: Vehicle Status, Original ETA, Reforecast ETA, Vehicle Model, Dealer Code, Haulier Name (e.g., ECM, GBA, BCA), Port/Site Location (e.g., GBA Grimsby).

SLI Prerequisites for VIP Access

A vehicle will not appear in VIP until all three of the following conditions are met in SLI: Status Code 40 (vehicle arrived at UK port); an actual transport order has been raised (viewable under the Dates tab); the Compound Entry Date is populated (indicates the vehicle is at the UK port and ready for hauler collection, viewable via the Red Truck icon).

Delivery Timeline: once a vehicle shows as Status 40 in SLI, it typically takes approximately 10 working days to arrive at the Retailer.

Accessing and Navigating VIP

  1. Logging in: portal at portal.gbagroup.com/Account/Login. Log in using the brand access email/password provided by your trainer or team lead.
  2. Searching Pending Orders (in-transit vehicles): hover over Order Viewer, select Pending Orders, enter the VIN into the search bar, click the Magnifying Glass icon to search. Reforecast ETA turns green when the vehicle is ready to dispatch from site, indicating the date is at its highest accuracy.
  3. Searching Delivered Vehicles: hover over Order Viewer, select Vehicles Delivered, input the VIN and click the magnifying glass. View historic delivery data including Date Delivered, Model, Dealer Code, Haulier, and Port Site.

Order Cancellations & Delivery Stages

When an order is cancelled, actions depend on the vehicle's current status in VIP: before/at 'Called Off'/'In Load Lane' - transportation can still be halted; past 'Called Off' - transportation cannot be cancelled. Always contact Group Logistics to notify them of the cancellation. 'Called Off' means the vehicle has been selected from its held position at the UK Port to move into the load lane for transport.

articles.html:
What is a Vehicle Transfer?

Brand Support agents receive requests from the RDC network to transfer a vehicle from one site to another. This occurs when a vehicle is at an RDC location or on order by one retailer, and another retailer negotiates and agrees to take ownership of the vehicle.

Common Reasons for Transfers

  • Demo Vehicle Request: one RDC has a vehicle on site as a demo unit that is needed for a customer at another RDC.
  • Build Order Progression: an RDC has a vehicle on order further along in the build process, and another RDC's customer requires a vehicle sooner.
  • Customer Relocation: a customer moves house and prefers to collect their vehicle from a different site.

Important policy notes: transfers are not limited to the same investor group. A completed Transfer Form is mandatory from the RDC releasing the vehicle. It is strictly prohibited to perform a vehicle transfer action over the phone.

Processing the Transfer Form

When an RDC submits a transfer request, an e-form arrives in the team inbox.

Verification checklist: locate the vehicle in SLI using the VIN number; verify the origin/releasing RDC number and destination RDC number on the e-form match SLI; check the form notes to confirm whether customer tagging/details should remain attached during the transfer.

Step-by-Step SLI Transfer Procedure

  1. Retrieve the order details: open the vehicle detail screen in SLI, enter the VIN number to display the order, copy the Order Number.
  2. Access Order Management & Query: go to the Yellow Phone icon at the top menu, right-click, select Order Management. From the Order's Query Selection window, click Bulk Transfer under System Queries, then click Accept.
  3. Filter Order Criteria: click the Additional Criteria tab, enter the Order Number into both the From and To fields under the Order No box, click Accept.
  4. Execute Bulk Order Transfer: highlight the order line returned in the query results, right-click on the grey header area at the top of the grid, select Bulk order transfer.
  5. Assign New RDC & Finalize: in the Bulk Order Transfer pop-up, input the new RDC number into both the Destination Retailer and Delivery Retailer fields; check the box for Transfer Customer Information if specified on the e-form to retain customer details (if the car already has customer information, check the box; if not, skip this step); click Accept. Reply to the transfer form email confirming the transfer action has been completed, and log the interaction in your logging system.

articles.title: Electric Vehicle Charging: A Simple Guide
articles.html:
Charging an EV isn't as complicated as it might first seem, though it does introduce a few new concepts and routines compared to filling up with petrol or diesel. This guide covers how EV batteries operate, where you can power up, the mechanics of AC versus DC charging, and the key factors affecting your overall range.

Types of Electrified Vehicles

  • Mild Hybrid: small electric motor assists the combustion engine; motor-generator provides boosts using stored electricity. Not plug-in.
  • Full Hybrid: combines combustion engine + battery electric motor; can drive short distances on electric power; recharges via driving and regenerative braking. Not plug-in.
  • Plug-in Hybrid (PHEV): like a full hybrid but with a larger battery that can be charged from an external power source. Plug-in.
  • Battery Electric Vehicle (BEV): fully electric, no combustion engine, fuel tank, or tailpipe emissions. Plug-in.
  • Fuel Cell Electric Vehicle (FCEV): generates electricity onboard by combining hydrogen and oxygen, emits water vapour; refuelling infrastructure is limited. Hydrogen refuel, not plug-in.

Battery Technology & Driving Range

Lithium-Ion Battery Design: high-voltage systems (like VW's MEB platform) use modular pouch cells with stacked/folded layers in a flexible outer film. Core benefits: no memory effect, high cyclical resistance, low self-discharge, high energy density, zero mechanical maintenance.

Battery Degradation: over time, all batteries experience slight capacity loss from usage, age, and charge cycles. Accelerating factors: extreme temperatures, frequent rapid charging, aggressive driving.

Second Life Applications: when no longer suitable for driving, EV batteries are repurposed for dealer energy storage - cutting overhead by storing cheap overnight grid power, lowering carbon footprint by up to 50%, supporting fast chargers without costly grid transformer upgrades, and supporting fleet & solar integration.

Factors Impacting Driving Range: high impact - cold outside temperatures, high speeds/acceleration, uphill terrain, extra vehicle weight, battery age. Minor impact - climate control (heating/AC), electronics like radios/wipers/headlights.

AC vs. DC Charging

AC (Alternating Current): current changes direction periodically; slower charging limited by the car's on-board charger; typical locations home/workplace/supermarkets/destination car parks; generally cheaper per session.

DC (Direct Current): flows in one direction at constant voltage; fast to ultra-rapid charging; typical locations motorway service stations/dedicated charging hubs; more expensive per session.

Typical charging speeds: AC Type 1 - 3.7kW/7kW. AC Type 2 - 3.7kW/7kW/22kW (three-phase). DC CHAdeMO - 100kW/150kW. DC CCS - 50kW/150kW/350kW. DC Type 2 - 150kW/250kW.

What determines actual charging speed: the vehicle can never charge faster than the lower capacity of either the charger or the car's internal maximum limit; larger physical battery sizes require more time to fill; cold weather and heavy climate control usage while plugged in will throttle charging speeds.

Where Can You Charge?

At Home: home charging is the most convenient option. An EV can plug into a standard 3-pin domestic socket in an emergency (requires prior inspection by an electrician), but a dedicated home wallbox is the safest and most efficient choice for overnight replenishment.

In Public: the UK public charging infrastructure features over 121,000 public EV chargers across more than 46,731 locations, managed by various charge point operators (CPOs) including BP Pulse, GRIDSERVE, Pod Point, OHME, InstaVolt, FastNed, Osprey, and Shell Recharge. Ultra-rapid hubs (150kW+) are the fastest-growing segment.

Making Charging Affordable

  • Smart Tariffs: energy providers offer specialized EV tariffs with heavily discounted overnight electricity rates.
  • Charging Habits: treat your EV like a phone - top up overnight at home, use public AC destinations during the day when necessary.
  • Cost Efficiency: home charging is vastly cheaper per mile than public rapid charging, a fraction of the per-mile cost of petrol or diesel.

articles.title: Understanding Transmission Types: A Simple Guide
articles.html:
Every car needs a way to send power from the engine to the wheels - that's the job of the transmission, a set of gears connecting the engine to the drive shaft.

Key Terms

  • Gear: a set of toothed wheels that work together to alternate the speed of a vehicle.
  • Clutch: the mechanism that connects and disconnects the engine from the transmission, allowing gears to be changed smoothly.
  • Pferdestarke (PS): a German unit of power still used in car specs, measuring the power the engine can generate from turning fuel into energy.
  • Torque: expressed in Newton-metres (Nm), the amount of force the engine can produce to pull the vehicle forward.
  • Engine Displacement: the combined volume capacity of all cylinders, expressed in cc. Generally, higher = more power.
  • Powertrain: where power from the engine is sent - FWD, RWD, or 4WD.

Manual Transmission

Driver changes gears using a clutch pedal and gear stick. Advantages: cheaper to buy, lower maintenance costs, more direct control. Disadvantages: fewer vehicles available, tiresome in heavy traffic, requires precise clutch control on hills.

Automatic Transmission

Changes gears on its own without a clutch pedal. Advantages: easier in stop-and-go traffic, more variants available, smoother/quicker shifts. Disadvantages: generally more expensive, higher maintenance costs; in the UK, drivers who pass their test in an automatic must retake the test in a manual to earn a full unrestricted licence.

The Four Main Types of Automatic-Style Transmission

  • Traditional Automatic (Torque Converter Automatic): uses a fluid coupling (torque converter) between engine and gearbox instead of a mechanical clutch, giving smooth, gentle gear changes.
  • Direct Shift Gearbox (DSG): a dual-clutch transmission with two separate clutches handling alternating gears (odd/even); the next gear is pre-selected so shifts happen almost instantly. Blends manual fuel efficiency/control with automatic ease. Note: VWG only uses DSG transmissions among its automatic-style options today.
  • Continuous Variable Transmission (CVT): uses a belt-and-pulley system providing a single, variable gear ratio that adjusts smoothly and continuously - no distinct gear changes.
  • Automated Shift Gearbox (ASG): an automated manual transmission - automatic (Drive position) or manual (nudge +/-). Combines manual fuel economy with automatic ease. Note: this technology has been phased out of production.

All-Wheel Drive: 4Motion

Separate from the gearbox, 4Motion is Volkswagen's all-wheel-drive system. Distributes power between front and rear axles, activates the rear axle automatically when loss of traction occurs, continuously adjusts power distribution depending on driving conditions (wet roads, loose surfaces).

articles.title: Understanding the VWG Warranty: A Complete Guide
articles.html:
Volkswagen Group United Kingdom (VWG), covering Volkswagen, Audi, SEAT, Skoda, CUPRA, Volkswagen Commercial Vehicles, and Volkswagen Passenger Cars, offers a layered warranty structure protecting customers against manufacturing defects, body corrosion, workmanship issues, and breakdowns.

1. Standard Warranty

Vehicles purchased new from a VWG Authorised Retailer in the UK qualify for a comprehensive three-year warranty: Years 1 & 2 unlimited mileage, Year 3 limited to 60,000 miles.

How warranty repairs work: any defect must be reported to the Authorised Repairer network as soon as discovered; rectification work is carried out exclusively by the Authorised Repairer network; any part replaced during a warranty repair becomes the property of VWG; replaced parts are covered for the remaining unexpired period of the vehicle's original warranty; the customer completes any required forms/documentation. Overseas repairs in Year 3: work must be done by a VWG-approved foreign repairer, and the invoice must be presented to an approved UK repairer within 14 days for a refund.

2. Wear and Tear Policy

Parts whose lifespan is heavily influenced by driving style and external factors are limited to a six-month or 6,500-mile window: brake linings, disc pads, clutch release bearings, clutch pressure/centre plates (braking & drivetrain); light bulbs, key fob and alarm batteries (electrical & lighting); seat and backrest covers, floor coverings (cabin & interior); wiper blades, shock absorbers, tyres, spark plugs (visibility & ride).

3. Body Protection Warranty (Perforation Corrosion)

VWG guarantees the structural integrity of the vehicle's bodywork against perforation corrosion for 12 years from the date of first registration. Unlike surface corrosion, perforation corrosion starts inside a panel and works outward due to manufacturing origins.

Preconditions for a claim: must be reported to the Authorised Repairer network as soon as discovered, within the warranty period; the perforation must not have been caused by damage, neglect, insufficient care/maintenance, or external corrosion; all body repairs must be carried out promptly using manufacturer specifications, approved parts and procedures.

4. Authorized Network Workmanship Warranty

Separately from the vehicle's manufacturing warranty, VWG's Authorised Repairer network guarantees its own repair and servicing work for one year or 12,000 miles from the date the work was carried out. A workmanship repair is free when: the repair is a direct result of faulty workmanship by the Authorised Repairer; the issue is not due to normal wear and tear or exclusions; it's reported to the original repairing retailer immediately; the vehicle has not been investigated or repaired by any other mechanic.

5. Roadside Assistance Coverage by Brand

  • Audi: 36 months
  • SEAT: 12 months
  • Skoda: 36 months (sold pre-1 May 2025), 12 months (sold after 1 May 2025)
  • Volkswagen Commercial Vehicles: 36 months
  • Volkswagen Passenger Cars: 12 months (36 months for Touareg and ID. Range)
  • CUPRA: 12 months

Note: coverage for used vehicles varies by brand and is available via each brand's official website.

6. Electric Vehicle Battery Warranty

Fully electric Audi vehicles carry additional protection against battery degradation down to 70 per cent over a period of eight years or 100,000 miles. Buyer's tip: used EV buyers should note that original new-car performance figures do not always reflect real-world performance with older batteries.

articles.title: Service Campaign vs. Recall Comparison
articles.html:
Comparison

  • Trigger: Service Campaign - technical issues of the product. Recall - problems resulting in fatalities or severe harm to vehicle occupants/public.
  • Safety relation: Service Campaign - not directly related to safety or compliance. Recall - directly related to safety or compliance.
  • Notification: Service Campaign - customers are not notified. Recall - VWG UK sends notifications to registered owners of affected vehicles.
  • Action taken: Service Campaign - the retailer (RDC) addresses issues on the vehicle's next workshop visit. Recall - a definitive and urgent response to address the safety concern.
  • Data source: Service Campaign - not applicable. Recall - notified using information from the Driver and Vehicle Licensing Agency (DVLA).

Definitions

  • Service campaign: addresses technical issues not directly related to safety or compliance. Customers are not notified; issues are addressed by the RDC during the vehicle's next workshop visit.
  • Recall: issued when a vehicle problem could result in fatalities or severe harm to those in the vehicle or on the road. VWG UK notifies registered owners based on DVLA data.

articles.title: Understanding Vehicle Architecture: Body Styles, Pillars, and Powertrains
articles.html:
Roof Pillars

A: Windshield sides. B: Mid-cabin. C: Rear door. D: Extended rear (Estates/SUVs).

Core Styles

  • Saloon: 3-box design (4 doors, separate boot).
  • Hatchback: 2-box design (shared cabin/cargo area).
  • Estate (Avant): extended roofline to D-pillar for maximum cargo space (Audi calls this "Avant").
  • Coupe & Cabriolet: 2-door fixed roof vs. retractable soft-top.

Utility & Commercial

  • SUV: high ground clearance, rugged chassis.
  • MPV: people carrier (3 seating rows, 7+ seats).
  • Pickup/Crew Cab: open rear cargo bed (Crew Cab adds a 2nd row of seats).
  • Combi & High-Top: flexible passenger/cargo van vs. extended high-roof commercial van.

Powertrains

  • BEV (All-Electric): battery-only power.
  • PHEV (Plug-in Hybrid): switches between battery & combustion engine.
  • HEV (Hybrid): self-charges small battery while driving.
  • FCEV (Fuel Cell): generates electricity onboard from hydrogen.

articles.title: Vehicle Life Cycle (Full Process)
articles.html:
The end-to-end journey of a vehicle - from initial customer inquiry through manufacturing, logistics, and final handover.

Phase 1: Customer Engagement & Ordering

  1. Initial Enquiry: customer reaches out to request vehicle details and specifications.
  2. Retailer Visit: the customer visits the dealership showroom to inspect models and discuss pricing.
  3. Test Drive: customer evaluates the vehicle's performance on a road test.
  4. Order Placement: customer officially places the order and pays the required deposit.

Phase 2: Sourcing & Manufacturing

  1. Vehicle Availability Check: the retailer checks inventory in order - Retailer Stock, National Stock, Factory Stock.
  2. Vehicle Build: if stock is unavailable, the order is transmitted to the factory production department for manufacturing.

Phase 3: Transit & Quality Inspections

  1. Departure from Place of Origin: the completed vehicle leaves the factory and travels to the primary departure port.
  2. Arrival in Emden, Germany: the vehicle arrives at the hub in Emden. Inspection check: 1st Vehicle Damage Report (VDR) inspection.
  3. Transportation to the UK: the vehicle is loaded onto cargo vessels and shipped across to the United Kingdom.
  4. UK Port Arrival: the vehicle offloads at the designated UK port terminal.

Phase 4: Preparation & Delivery

  1. Transportation to the Retailer: the vehicle is loaded onto a carrier and delivered directly to the destination dealership.
  2. Arrival at the Retailer: the vehicle is offloaded at the retailer site. Inspection check: 3rd Vehicle Damage Report (VDR) inspection.
  3. Pre-Delivery Inspection (PDI): technicians verify custom factory specifications and perform technical checks - oil level verification, tyre pressure adjustments, programming service intervals in the Electronic Control Units (ECUs).
  4. Vehicle Registration & Policy Activation: official vehicle registration is completed, and warranty/service policies are activated.
  5. Vehicle Handover: documentation, keys, and vehicle are presented to the customer, who signs off confirming the vehicle has been received in good condition.

articles.title: Vehicle De-Tag & Deregistration Guide
articles.html:
For the de-tag steps, see Steps to De-Tag A Vehicle.

Overview

A "de-tag" is the administrative process of unlinking a specific vehicle from one customer in SLI so it can be reassigned to another customer or converted for stock-ordering purposes. Primary rule: a vehicle can only be de-tagged if it has not yet been registered.

Vehicle Deregistration Rules

If a retailer needs to make a formal request to deregister a vehicle, the application must be submitted within 7 working days of the registration date. Note: deregistration is an extra-statutory concession and is never guaranteed.

Automatic disqualification criteria - deregistration will strictly not be allowed if: the vehicle was registered directly in the retailer's name; the vehicle was registered to an associated, parent, or subsidiary company (including associated leasing companies or car hire firms); the vehicle has been used (e.g., driven off the retailer's forecourt).

Reasons for rejecting de-tag: incorrect process (did not follow the correct de-tag rules); no proof/evidence/insufficient evidence; WLTP mismatch (error received when de-tagging); pre part reg (part registered vehicle); over 7 days (Motability must not be over 7 days).

Deregistration process: only the original registering retailer may apply; submit DVLA Form V996 (downloadable via GOV.UK).

Brand-Specific De-Tag Requirements

Volkswagen Commercial Vehicles (VWCV)

Required documentation: Status 10 or below - no documentation required. Status 20 or above - requires one of: Original Order Form, Formal Cancellation Letter.

Special handling for ID. Buzz & ID. Buzz Cargo: because of crossover with VW Passenger Cars, these models do not use standard forms. Direct the RDC to complete HUB form CV0678-22 (ID. Buzz De-Tag Request Form). Reject all other form submissions.

Audi

General rules: Status 36-40 (without Transport Order) - must add a protected from mandatory block EDE for 24 hours. Order Types 03, 09, & 11 (Status 30 and under) - transfer the vehicle to 64001. Critical: ensure the call-off is cancelled prior to transferring, or a Transport Order will raise automatically upon UK arrival and ship the vehicle on-site.

Restricted & special models: RS & GT E-tron models always require formal cancellation documents. Exclusive Paint vehicles may be de-tagged but must remain at the centre. Escalate to Supply Team (SLTQUESTIONS@AUDI.co.uk) for RS 4 Avant Competition and RS3 Competition - CSC cannot de-tag these directly (note: if a customer pulls out of the sale, the Centre will be charged £2,000.00 + VAT).

Volkswagen Passenger Cars

Required documentation: Status 10 or below - no documentation required. Status 20 or above - RDC must supply at least one of: cancellation document, original order or Motability cancellation screenshot, VWFS finance decline letter or original agreement form.

Block & status procedures: Status 36-40 - de-tag to Status 07, then apply both the Protected From Mandatory Block and EDE block for 24 hours. This prevents the vehicle from returning to the general stockholding pot and holds it for customer reallocation.

ID. Models (BEV) Grant Option Checks: before de-tagging any ID model, check the Options Box for codes W25, S7C, SV7. If any of these codes are present, email the order number to VWPRODMKTG@Volswagen.co.uk to remove the grant option before executing the de-tag.

articles.title: Quoting Process
articles.html:
Purpose of Vehicle Quotations

Retailer Development Centres (RDCs) contact the Customer Service Centre (CSC) to request price quotes. While the majority of quotation calls originate from Audi, other brands occasionally request quotes too. Price Verification: RDCs request quotes after taking an order to ensure accurate pricing to their end customer. Stock Checks: retailers may see a vehicle in another retailer's stock and wish to verify if the pricing figures are correct.

Quoting Process

  1. Enter the order number on the Vehicle Details screen.
  2. If the order is at status 40 without a transport order, apply three blocks to the order to prevent a transportation order from being raised (removed at the end of the quotation).
  3. Right-click on the Vehicle Details screen and select Order Modification.
  4. Ask the retailer for the order type, then select the relevant option (most likely 09 or 08).
  5. Complete the details under the yellow Quote button.
  6. Enter 12 in the Months section and 0 in the Weeks section, then save.
  7. In the PO button, enter TBA.
  8. Click the Customer Entry tab at the top of SLI.
  9. Ask the retailer for the customer type, as well as the first RFO and second RFO.
  10. When adding the second RFO, you may be prompted to enter COMP details - set the company to N/A.
  11. Enter the POS postcode as MK14 5AN.
  12. Set the telephone details to 0 and save the screen - this is a default address.
  13. Set the handover date to the end of the month, then save.
  14. Once all details are added, click the yellow telephone, then click the pound sign.
  15. Provide the total price and quotation number to the retailer. Once the pricing details have been shared, de-tag the vehicle.

articles.title: Vehicle Unadoption Process
articles.html:
Overview

The Unadopt process (only unadopt a vehicle if it's getting tagged to a demo or agency + Quotation process) is used when a retailer needs to be refunded for a vehicle so they can access additional funding discounts - for example, putting it on a funded demo plan, getting discounted terms on an agency/fleet vehicle, or transferring it to another RDC while still adopted with the current retailer. Brand Support agents process these requests as they arrive from the RDC network for vehicles physically on-site.

1. Receiving the Request

Requests arrive as an E-form, submitted via the Volkswagen Hub, landing in Brand Support's Outlook. Key fields on the E-form: Requestor, Centre name/number, Full VIN, Model, Request reason, Explanation. Tip: the Explanation field is where transfer instructions and destination retailer numbers usually live - read it closely.

2. Eligibility Checks - Rules

Always check: the reason stated on the E-form; retailer numbers match between the E-form and SLI.

Do NOT unadopt if: transfer type shows A (already transferred while adopted); vehicle invoiced (adopted) today (must wait until the next day); partially/fully registered with no demo plan number (RDC must abort & resubmit first).

3. Process the Unadopt - SLI

  1. Read the E-form - confirm RDC number + reason (note any transfer request).
  2. In SLI: Vehicle -> Vehicle Detail.
  3. Copy the VIN into SLI.
  4. Check the order status: Adopted (screen turns yellow, code shown in Retailer Inv. box) - continue; Not adopted - stop, see next section.

If NOT adopted: reply to the RDC declining the request; move the E-form to unadopts@vwg.co.uk marked Rejected.

If adopted, continue in GIS: log in to GIS; click Documents; select Consignment/Invoices of chassis; enter VIN then Browse; tick line 'I' then Return Invoice; complete cancellation fields (Currency code GBP, Cancellation reason CRIR, GIS action RC, SLI Action B, Type of location 0=stays put/2=transferring, New Location if transferring = new 5-digit retailer number); click Perform cancelation.

4. Transfer the Vehicle (if requested)

  1. Yellow phone icon -> Order Management.
  2. Bulk Transfer -> Accept.
  3. Additional Criteria tab.
  4. Enter the Order number in both From and To.
  5. Accept.
  6. Select the order line (turns blue).
  7. Right-click grey area -> Bulk Order Transfer.
  8. Enter 5-digit destination RDC code.
  9. Tick "Transfer Customer Information".
  10. Accept.
  11. Yes.
  12. Vehicle is now unadopted & transferred.

Critical: skipping step 9 will automatically de-tag the customer, and a price change may apply. Never skip this tick box. (For transfer steps, see Vehicle Transfers Guide.)

5. Add an Order Note

  1. SLI -> vehicle order -> Dates tab.
  2. Click the scroll and pen icon.
  3. Add a note, e.g. "Vehicle unadopted and transferred, ZH 26/6/2026".

6. Set the Forward Sale Date

Set to end of current month. Worked example: E-form received 26 June 2026; Type Stock (untagged); Consignment date 26 February 2026; Rtlr. Inv. Date 24 June 2026; New forward sale date 26 July 2026.

7. Remove the Invoice Block

Returning the invoice auto-triggers a block - this always needs manual removal.

  1. Right-click grey area on main Vehicle screen.
  2. Vehicle block / Author Maint.
  3. Select Invoice block.
  4. Delete.
  5. Accept.

Quick Checklist

  • Reason & retailer numbers match E-form + SLI
  • No disqualifying conditions apply
  • Vehicle confirmed adopted (yellow + Retailer Inv. code)
  • Return invoice processed in GIS with correct fields
  • Transfer completed - Transfer Customer Information ticked
  • Order note added in SLI
  • Forward sale date recalculated
  • Invoice block deleted

articles.title: Making a vehicle amendment
articles.html:
When Can an Amendment Be Made?

Vehicle amendments can only be made up to a specific stage in the order process: permitted while the vehicle order is in its early stages (before Status 20); cut-off point is Status 20 - once an order reaches Status 20, amendments are no longer possible, because the vehicle is typically scheduled for production with a confirmed build week, so no further specification or order adjustments can be processed by the factory.

Vehicle amendments will not be completed over the telephone unless a valid configuration code is provided by the RDC. If the RDC cannot provide a configuration code (e.g. technical issues), they must email the UK specialist team so the order can be adjusted manually.

Rule summary: before Status 20 - process amendment normally in SLI. Status 20 or later (confirmed build week) - locked, refuse amendment. Phone request with a valid configuration code - execute requested adjustments over the phone. Phone request with no code/system issue - do not process over the phone, direct RDC to email the UK specialist team.

Step-by-step (SLI)

  1. Ask for the order number. In SLI, select the brand first, then enter the order number.
  2. Check the status code: if before 20, proceed; if 20 and above, reject the request.
  3. Once you have found the order, right-click on the screen.
  4. From the menu, navigate to Order Modification. The screen will change to show the current vehicle specification.
  5. Enter the configuration code in the Config. Code field.
  6. Click the magnifying glass icon.
  7. To save the order changes, click Save.

Final check: after saving the amendment, ask the RDC to confirm the changes before ending the call.

articles.html:

  1. Open the vehicle order in the SLI system.
  2. Click the audit trail icon (the small folder-and-chart graphic).
  3. Estimate a rough timeframe for when the amendment was made.
  4. On the history screen, locate the Movement Description column.
  5. Scan the list for Vehicle Specification Entry.

  7. Review the new window that shows the exact changes made.

  9. Locate the User column that contains the dealer portal number.
  10. Note the specific user ID number assigned to that movement.
  11. Cross-reference that number with the dealer portal user list provided by your facilitator.

articles.title: Electric Mobility (E-Mobility) & EV Fundamentals
articles.html:
Overview & Environmental Impact

E-Mobility refers to electric powertrain technologies and the connected infrastructure that enable the electric propulsion of vehicles and fleets.

  • Zero Direct Emissions: fully electric vehicles emit 0 grams of CO2, directly reducing greenhouse gases.
  • Urban Air Quality: reduces local exhaust pollution, helping improve air quality in densely populated cities.
  • Sustainable Energy: EVs can be powered using 100% renewable energy sources.

The EV Spectrum (Vehicle Types)

  • mHEV (Mild Hybrid Electric Vehicle): features a 48V electrical network to support the internal combustion engine.
  • HEV (Hybrid Electric Vehicle / Full Hybrid): combines an engine with a self-charging electric motor system.
  • PHEV (Plug-in Hybrid Electric Vehicle): switches between battery and combustion power, with a battery that recharges via an external plug.
  • BEV (Battery Electric Vehicle): 100% fully electric, powered solely by high-voltage batteries.

Technical Advantages & Efficiency

  • High Energy Efficiency: electric motors achieve 90-95% efficiency, compared to only 25-30% efficiency in internal combustion engines (ICE).
  • Instant Torque: delivers maximum torque immediately from a standstill, enabling strong acceleration.
  • Regenerative Braking: recovers energy during deceleration to recharge the high-voltage battery, improving efficiency in city traffic.
  • 30% Lower Maintenance: service and maintenance costs are roughly 30% lower than those for ICE vehicles.

VWG Strategy: "The Future Drives Electrically"

Global Leader Ambition: Volkswagen Group (VWG) has launched the world's largest EV offensive to become the global market leader in e-mobility.

  • 35 Billion Euro Investment committed to e-mobility development.
  • Delivery Goals: following 572,100 fully electric vehicles delivered in 2022, VWG is on track for a 20% BEV market share.
  • 50 New BEVs by 2030: around 50 brand-new fully electric models will be launched by 2030.
  • 60 Hybrid Portfolio: expanding to around 60 hybrid models by the end of the decade (over half are already in production).

Myth vs Fact

  • Myth: "EVs are complex to maintain." Fact: reduced complexity - removes mechanical components like oil systems, exhausts, and clutches.
  • Myth: "EVs require frequent servicing." Fact: fewer moving parts - far fewer routine service items compared to petrol vehicles.
  • Myth: "EV downtime is unpredictable." Fact: predictable schedules - preventative software checks and fewer wear components support consistent maintenance schedules.

Ownership & Customer Experience

  • Effortless & Calm Driving: a smoother, whisper-quiet drive that reduces stress during rush-hour commutes and school runs.
  • Enjoyment & Personal Satisfaction: a sense of pride in driving a modern, rewarding vehicle aligned with personal values.
  • Reliability & Purpose: confidence in advanced technology while contributing to a cleaner future for the next generation.

articles.title: EV Battery Systems
articles.html:
Key Components of EV Battery Systems

Battery Architecture (Hierarchy)

An electric vehicle (EV) battery is built in layers, moving from individual units up to the full power system.

  • Cell: the foundational unit of a lithium-ion battery. Core components: Cathode (+), Anode (-), and Electrolyte.
  • Module: a clustered group of cells connected in series and parallel to achieve the targeted voltage and energy capacity.
  • Pack: the final, complete assembly installed in the vehicle. Contains: battery modules/cells, control software, structural housing, and environmental systems.

Control & Management Systems

1. Battery Management System (BMS)

Function: the onboard computer responsible for real-time monitoring and regulation. Key tasks: ensures safe, balanced, and optimal charging and discharging across all cells.

2. Thermal Management System

Function: regulates the physical operating environment of the battery. Key tasks: provides targeted heating and cooling to maintain optimal performance and prolong battery life.

Safety Systems

Safety Disconnect

Function: high-voltage circuit breaker mechanism. Key tasks: automatically or manually isolates power from the battery during severe faults, accidents, or maintenance to prevent fires and electrical hazards.
